principles.title: Rest interval duration and strength adaptations
principles.summary: Systematic review: trained individuals generally appear to benefit from longer inter-set rest (>2 min) when the goal is to maximize strength, although meaningful gains can occur with shorter rests.

principles.title: Longer inter-set rest in resistance-trained men
principles.source: Schoenfeld et al., Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research, 2016
principles.summary: In a small randomized trial of trained men, 3-min rest produced greater strength gains than 1-min rest and some hypertrophy outcomes also favored the longer-rest condition.

principles.title: Short vs long rest and hypertrophy
principles.source: Grgic et al., European Journal of Sport Science, 2017
principles.summary: Systematic review found no evidence that short rest is required for hypertrophy; longer rest can help preserve training volume.

principles.title: Volume load versus rest interval
principles.source: Longo et al., Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research, 2022
principles.summary: When volume load was considered, maintaining load/volume appeared more important than using a specific rest interval. Rest is therefore treated as a performance-preservation tool, not a magic hypertrophy variable.

engineering_notes: Rest targets are evidence-informed heuristics, not a validated personal prescription.
The engine gives ranges rather than a single mandatory number.
Longer rest is not automatically penalized when it preserves quality; excessively short rest is flagged when performance drops.

Calisthenics static-skill rest recommendations are extrapolated from strength/power recovery principles because direct high-quality normative research for advanced planche/front-lever training is limited.
